To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NMDA antagonists infused into the dorsolater striatum impair the initial acquisition of an egocentirc response discrimination.
the NMDA receptor antagonist AP-5 (25 nmol) impaired the acquisition of an egocentic response discrimination in the cross-maze.
the competitive NMDA receptor antagonist, AP-5, impaired acquisition of a response discrimination, but not response reversal learning, when injected into the dorsomedial striatum of rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neurobiological mechanisms that underlie the acquisition and expression of egocentric responses.
the neural basis of learning and memory, with a special interest in the role of the basal ganglia in the acquisition, expression and extinction of learned responses.
the role of the basal ganglia in the learning of response discrimination tasks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NMDA antagonism in the dorsolatral striatum is not necessary for the reversal learning process.
NMDA receptor antagonism in the dorsolaterl striatum impairs acquisition but not reversal learning in a modified cross maze.
NMDA receptor blockade in the dorsolaterl striatum impairs the initial learning of a response but not reversal learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NMDA receptor activation in the dorsolatal striatum is important for the acquisition of an egocenrtic response discrimination, but not the reversal of that discrimination.

the dorsolateral and ventromedial striatum are important for the initial acquisition of an egocentic response discrimination and that the dorsomedial striatum is important for the reversal learning of the egocentric response.
the NMDA receptors are important for the acquisition of a new response but not for the reversal of an existing response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NMDA receptor antagonism in the striatum impairs egocentric learning.
NMDA receptor blockade in the dorsolater striatum impairs response acquisition, but not response reversal learning.
the dorsolateral region of the striatum plays a role in egocentric learning and that this role may depend on NMDA receptor function.
